notices.short_title: Health and Fitness Program for Justice-Involved Youth
notices.description: Through this Request for Proposals (RFP), ACS is seeking a qualified vendor to provide health and fitness programming to justice-involved youth. The programs would engage housed youth detained and/or remanded at ACS detention facilities in rigorous physical activity as well as in health and wellness educational programming in accordance with the Center for Disease Controls (CDC) recommendation for adolescents to engage in regular daily, mostly moderate or vigorous intensity, aerobic physical activity.
notices.plain: The Administration for Children's Services awarded Cysero LLC a $2,555,190 contract to provide health and fitness programming, including physical activity and wellness education, for justice-involved youth held at its detention facilities.

notices.short_title: Therapeutic and Creative Expression Youth Training Program
notices.plain: The Administration for Children's Services awarded Keshad Donte Adeniyi a $155,000 contract for a therapeutic and creative expression youth training program, using a noncompetitive small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business.
The Board of Elections intends to award a negotiated contract for electronic ballot accessibility services, with responses due Nov. 25, 2026.

notices.short_title: SMD_Services_IDIQ Contract for Mold Remediation at Various NYCHA Developments, Citywide
notices.description:
Scope of Work: The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and qualified personnel necessary to perform mold remediation, plumbing, electrical, and general construction repairs within the apartment. Work shall include identifying and fixing all sources of leaks, and moisture issues; repairing plumbing; replacing damaged caulking, grout, surrounds, and pipe insulation, inspecting hidden wall and ceiling for hidden mold, removing mold, and restoring all affected walls, ceilings, floors, and interior finishes.

Contract Term: 3 years  from the award date on NYCHAs Purchase Order.  NYCHA, in its sole discretion, shall have the option to extend the Term of this Contract for up to two one-year renewals.

Bid Security
notices.plain: The New York City Housing Authority is seeking competitive sealed bids, due Dec. 24, 2026, for an indefinite-quantity contract to remediate mold, fix leaks and make related plumbing, electrical and interior repairs at various apartments in NYCHA developments citywide, for a three-year term with up to two one-year extensions.

notices.description:
The Office of Facilities Development is seeking proposals for a range of critical professional services to support the needs of its Facility Management Department in the areas of small-scale urgent sourcing and payments, provision of expert facility management as required, and provision of as-needed key staff to support facility operations.

 

The Vendor shall be responsible to provide: 

 

  1. Expedited procurement, payment and cost management services of urgent goods and services, all as described further in this SOW (the 'Services'').
  2. Facilities maintenance support services with respect to certain healthcare facilities…
notices.plain: NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals through a Request for Proposals from vendors to provide facility management services, including urgent purchasing and payment help, expert facility management and key staff to support facility operations, with responses due Dec. 28, 2026.

notices.description: NYC Health + Hospitals consists of buildings and infrastructure of various ages and conditions across its many campuses. As the patient base has increased and the methods of delivering care has changed, the buildings, many of which are decades old, have to be constantly upgraded or replaced. This growth has driven the growth of the total square feet of the system to be maintained to over 20,000,000 sq. ft. The Office of Facilities Development (OFD) is responsible for maintenance and operations of all campuses and buildings to ensure the clinicians have the facilities needed to deliver care. Campuses within the network range in size from a few thousand to over a 1 million square feet emphasizing the need for a new and robust Facilities Management and Asset Information System (FMIS) with the capability and capacity to organize, identify, and manage all infrastructure assets. This project entails the procurement and implementation of an industry-standard FMIS solution that will fulfill the business requirements of the Health System.
notices.plain: NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals from vendors to buy and set up a new facilities management and asset information system to track and manage its buildings and infrastructure, with responses due Dec. 28, 2026.

notices.short_title: Technical Assistance Services for Organizational Development
notices.description: DYCD's capacity-building and technical assistance programs support DYCDs contracted providers in various areas needed to enhance program services. DYCD is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) in the areas of Organization Development, Fiscal Management, Strength-Based Approaches to Service Delivery, Career Development, Developing a Safe and Supportive Environment, Adult Literacy Support, Mental Health Support and Case Management. These services have been determined to be of high need to support our contracted providers and the work they do for the City of New York.

notices.short_title: Notice of Ratification for Minor Rules Violation Pursuant to §1-11 of the Concession rules of the City of New York for CODI-2027
notices.description:
On November 16, 2026, pursuant to §1-11(a)(ii) of Title 12 of the Rules of the City of New York (the Concession Rules), the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation (MRV) request made on October 29, 2026 by the New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) that took place with regard to the above-referenced request for Franchise and Concession Review Committee approval for DEP to negotiate a significant concession agreement with Waste Management of NY, LLC for the expansion of the co-digestion program Newtown Creek. 

 

The violation occurred with regard to §1-16(b)(4) of the Concession Rules, which requires that DEP notify each affected community board and Borough President office of the agencys intent to seek FCRC approval for a Different Procedure and simultaneously post said notice on the Citys website. DEP issued the notice to the community board and Borough President for this concession on October 26, 2026; however, it did not simultaneously post the notice on the…
notices.plain: The Department of Environmental Protection reported that its failure to post a required notice on the city website, on a proposed Newtown Creek co-digestion concession with Waste Management of NY, LLC, was ratified as a minor rules violation on Nov. 16, 2026.
